root_cause.text: In the ab8500_charger driver, IRQ handlers were requested (via devm_) before the power_supply device was registered (via devm_), leading to a use-after-free during device removal because devm_ frees resources in reverse order, and a potential use of an uninitialized power_supply pointer if an interrupt fires during probe.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the interrupt handler... This will lead to the IRQ handler calling `power_supply_changed()` with a freed `power_supply` handle." The patch moves the entire interrupt request block to after the power_supply registration (see diff: the IRQ loop is removed from before registration and added after registration).

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 1c1f13a006ed0d71bb5664c8b7e3e77a28da3beb
Author: Linus Walleij <linusw@kernel.org>
Date:   Sun May 23 00:50:39 2021 +0200

    power: supply: ab8500: Move to componentized binding
    
    The driver has problems with the different components of
    the charging code racing with each other to probe().
    
    This results in all four subdrivers populating battery
    information to ascertain that it is populated for their
    own needs for example.
    
    Fix this by using component pr
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit shows that in the new probe() function, IRQ handlers are requested via devm_request_threaded_irq (lines ~3452) BEFORE the power supply devices are registered via devm_power_supply_register (lines ~3570-3583). This violates the proper ordering required to prevent use-after-free/uninitialized pointer access: an interrupt could fire between IRQ registration and power supply registration, accessing uninitialized psy pointers. Additionally, during removal, devm_ frees resources in reverse order, so power supplies (registered later) are freed before IRQs, leading to potential use-after-free if an IRQ fires after supply removal. The previous code had the correct ordering (supplies first, then IRQs), and this commit reverses it, thus introducing the vulnerability. No fix is present; the ordering is still incorrect.
